title: Emrys and the Uniform
premise: In 1913, apprentice clockmaker Coral Ashgrove is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock in the garrison town of Vellmarsh, where he discovers a hidden ledger inside the clockworks recording every name the army has requisitioned, conscripted, or erased. When soldiers occupy the town and seize all records, Coral must smuggle the ledger past three checkpoints to reach a journalist in the capital, aided by Emrys Hale, a young officer whose uniform marks him as the enemy but whose conscience pulls the other way. Their alliance deepens into love that both know duty forbids. The plan costs them the observatory, an old mentor, and nearly their lives; Coral delivers the ledger at last, and though the town's names are restored and the officers disgraced, he and Emrys survive only by choosing each other over every rank and rule they were born to obey.
about_author: Lena Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing requisition records from occupied European towns before turning to fiction. She writes historical novels about ordinary people caught in machinery larger than themselves.

chapters.title: The Master Clock Stops
chapters.summary: Coral Ashgrove, POV. Summoned to Vellmarsh's hilltop observatory to repair its failing master clock, Coral finds gears deliberately jammed around a hidden compartment. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath professional pride, as ten years of learned silences tell him someone wanted this clock stopped.

chapters.title: Names in the Works
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Inside the compartment he finds a ledger listing hundreds of townsfolk marked for requisition, conscription, or erasure, kept by the late head horologist. Emotional beat: dawning dread; Coral realizes his craft has handed him something people died to hide.

chapters.title: Requisition Orders
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Army columns enter Vellmarsh overnight; notices demand all ledgers and registers be surrendered by week's end. His landlady's name appears on a posted list. Emotional beat: the town's ordinary rhythms shatter, and Coral must decide whether silence still keeps anyone safe.

chapters.title: An Officer at the Door
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Lieutenant Emrys Hale arrives to inventory the observatory and catches Coral with the ledger half-hidden in his coat. Instead of arresting him, Emrys pockets it and walks away. Emotional beat: shock and wary gratitude; Coral cannot tell if he's been spared or trapped.

chapters.title: What the Uniform Owes
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Emrys returns alone at night, revealing his father was erased by the same system and that he enlisted to find out why. He proposes Coral carry the ledger out while he falsifies the inventory. Emotional beat: reluctant trust between two men trained never to give it.

chapters.title: The Clockmaker's Oath
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Coral studies the checkpoint routes with old mentor Tobias Wrenn, who once taught him which silences protect people. Wrenn refuses to flee, insisting someone respectable must stay behind. Emotional beat: Coral accepts the mission not as heroism but as repayment of a decade of shelter.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: The Bridge
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Disguised as a courier of clock parts, Coral passes the bridge checkpoint by hiding the ledger inside a disassembled regulator case, using a soldier's ignorance of mechanisms against him. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into fear when he realizes the search will tighten next time.

chapters.title: Lessons After Curfew
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Emrys teaches Coral military protocol and forged pass procedures in the observatory after dark. Between drills, they speak honestly for the first time. Emotional beat: intimacy growing in stolen hours, each aware the uniform between them could become a wall at any moment.

chapters.title: The List Gets Longer
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. New postings appear; Wrenn's name is added for 'obstruction.' Coral copies pages of the ledger into miniature code on watch faces. Emotional beat: grief hardening into resolve as survival becomes indistinguishable from resistance.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: The Garrison Gate
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. At the garrison gate a sharp-eyed sergeant recognizes Coral's tools as belonging to the observatory. Emrys intervenes, claiming Coral under official repair orders, burning his own credibility to do it. Emotional beat: rescue laced with guilt; Coral sees what Emrys is spending to shield him.

chapters.title: Found Family in a Wine Cellar
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Hiding below a smuggler's tavern, Coral meets the network moving erased people out of Vellmarsh: a printer, a nun, two children. They treat him as one of their own. Emotional beat: warmth he never permitted himself, and terror that his mission endangers them all.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Emrys is questioned about the missing ledger by Colonel Vasse, who suspects but lacks proof. Emrys lies fluently and hates how easily it comes. Emotional beat: the cost of double life made visible; duty and conscience can no longer share a body.

chapters.title: Wrenn's Last Wind
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Wrenn is arrested for tampering with posted lists. Before the guards take him, he winds the observatory clock one final time and tells Coral, 'A mechanism only fails when someone stops trusting it.' Emotional beat: farewell as inheritance; the mentor passes the work on.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: The Mountain Road
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. The mountain road checkpoint is a trap; Vasse has leaked word of a courier. Coral abandons the ledger's hiding place and memorizes nothing, carrying it openly as a grieving apprentice transporting his master's effects. Emotional beat: the boldest lie is truth, worn like armor through shaking hands.

chapters.title: The Letter That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Emrys intercepts orders to execute Wrenn and forge documents implicating the observatory network. He burns them, knowing discovery means a firing squad. Emotional beat: point of no return; Emrys stops being a man inside the machine and becomes a saboteur of it.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Tavern
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. The wine cellar network is raided; the children escape through Coral's quick rerouting of a dumbwaiter, but the printer is taken and the ledger's existence confirmed to Vasse. Emotional beat: devastation and self-blame, found family scattered by his own mission.

chapters.title: Two Fugitives
chapters.summary: Emrys and Coral, alternating. Stripped of rank and hunted together, they flee across country toward the capital, arguing, confessing, and finally admitting what they are to each other. Emotional beat: love declared plainly at last, precisely because everything else has been stripped away.

chapters.title: The Capital's Long Corridors
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. In the capital they hunt the journalist, Aldous Merrin, through ministries that stonewall them. Merrin agrees to publish only with verification. Emotional beat: bureaucratic despair; the truth is worthless without someone powerful enough to be afraid of it.

chapters.title: Vasse Closes In
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Vasse's men corner them at Merrin's print shop. Emrys holds the stairway while Coral escapes with the ledger, taking a bullet in the shoulder. Emotional beat: climax of sacrifice; Emrys chooses Coral's survival over his own without hesitation.

chapters.title: Publication
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. The ledger runs in full; names are restored, warrants issued for Vasse, and the occupation collapses under scandal. Coral sits vigil at the prison hospital where Emrys lies wounded. Emotional beat: victory that feels like aftermath; justice arrived, but slowly and at cost.

chapters.title: The Clock Runs Again
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Coral rebuilds the master clock, installing Wrenn's name on a brass plate inside the case. Freed townsfolk gather to hear it strike. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into craft; the mechanism trusts again because someone kept faith with it.

chapters.title: Emrys and the Uniform
chapters.summary: Emrys and Coral, shared close. Emrys hangs his uniform in the observatory as a relic and takes work repairing the town's smaller clocks beside Coral. Emotional beat: resolution and quiet joy; they have paid the price of survival and found that love, unlike duty, asks only to be kept wound.
